# Flim — Style Reference

> Contact sheet on a light table, marked with one yellow grease-pencil dot. Swizzy at 160px over a white canvas, a faint graph-paper grid in #e9e9e9, near-black #141414 for every stroke, and color left to the film frames.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Flim speaks a contact-sheet editorial language. It runs on a #ffffff Paper Canvas, with #f5f5f5 Fog Surface for the hero grid and product frame, #e9e9e9 Mist Rule for graph-paper lines and chip wells, and #141414 Ink for 479 text elements and every filled button. The chromatic budget is four decorative hues, #fecc33, #30a81d, #21935b and #ff8400. They are rationed to inline glyph tiles and cursor avatars, while the film stills supply every other color on the page and no action carries a hue. The typography thesis is polarity. Swizzy at weight 500 with a uniform -0.02em tracking runs from 24px body to a 160px display, and PP Neue Montreal Mono answers it at 12px, uppercase, +0.06em. The scale leaps 2.76× between its top two steps instead of climbing a conventional 1.25 ladder. Shape is mostly square-cut stills and 4px or 8px buttons punctuated by 160px pills. Elevation is tonal rather than shadowed. The result reads as a film archive's index card rather than a software dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page background, logo marquee band, white search button and reversed text on Ink (95 text uses) — the empty white that lets 160px type and stills breathe. |
| Fog Surface | `#f5f5f5` | `--color-fog-surface` | Graph-paper hero field, product mockup frame and inline glyph tiles (22 uses) — a one-step tonal lift that replaces shadows as the elevation signal. |
| Mist Rule | `#e9e9e9` | `--color-mist-rule` | Grid lines on the hero field, filter-chip fills and the search well (15 uses) — the line work of the system, drawn as fills rather than borders. Do not use it for text. |
| Ink | `#141414` | `--color-ink` | All headlines, body, mono labels, sign-up fills and stat pills (479 text uses, 42 fills) — a softened black that is the entire voice and the only action color. |
| Frosted Glass | `#ffffff1a` | `--color-frosted-glass` | Translucent chips and hover wells laid over Ink surfaces (3 uses) — a 10% white veil that separates layers on dark without adding a new gray. |
| Pewter Veil | `#d9d9d91a` | `--color-pewter-veil` | Secondary translucent overlay on stills and dark panels (2 uses) — a cooler sibling of Frosted Glass for a second glass layer. Do not use it on the white canvas. |
| Sunbeam Dot | `#fecc33` | `--color-sunbeam-dot` | The yellow disc inside headline glyph tiles and the hero CTA thumbnail backdrop (6 uses) — the grease-pencil mark, decorative only. Do not promote it to a button fill. |
| Sprout Signal | `#30a81d` | `--color-sprout-signal` | Cursor avatars and live-presence markers in collaborative mockups (6 uses) — a status-flavored green that signals people in the frame. Do not use it for success states in forms. |
| Forest Play | `#21935b` | `--color-forest-play` | Double play-arrow glyphs and the "Me" cursor bubble (2 uses) — a deeper green that reads as a transport control. Decorative only. |
| Ember Tick | `#ff8400` | `--color-ember-tick` | Small orange markers inside product illustrations (3 uses) — the warmest note in the set, reserved for annotation. Do not use it as a link or CTA color. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Swizzy — the single grotesk voice for display, body and navigation · `--font-swizzy`

- **Substitute:** Inter Display at 600, Geist at 500, Hanken Grotesk at 600. Swizzy draws a touch heavier than its nominal 500, so Inter-family cuts need one step up to match the stroke at 160px.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 700
- **Sizes:** 16px, 24px, 32px, 38px, 58px, 160px
- **Line height:** 0.86 (160px), 1.0 (16px, 32px), 1.1 (24px, 58px), 1.16 (38px)
- **Letter spacing:** -3.2px at 160px, -1.16px at 58px, -0.64px at 32px, -0.48px at 24px, 0px at 16px and 38px
- **Role:** Weight 500 does nearly all the work (363 uses). The face is never bolded for emphasis, so a 160px headline and a 24px paragraph share one stroke character and differ only in size. The -0.02em tracking is constant across every size from 24px up, which is anti-convention, since most systems tighten only the display steps. The scale reads 24 → 32 as a Perfect Fourth (1.333) and then jumps 2.76× from 58px to 160px, so the top of the page shouts in a way a Major Third ladder would forbid.

### PP Neue Montreal Mono — the uppercase technical label and search voice · `--font-pp-neue-montreal-mono`

- **Substitute:** Geist Mono at 400, DM Mono at 400, IBM Plex Mono at 400. Neue Montreal Mono draws light and narrow, so do not use Space Mono or JetBrains Mono, which read noticeably heavier.
- **Weights:** 400, 500
- **Sizes:** 9px, 12px, 16px
- **Line height:** 1.0
- **Letter spacing:** 0.54px at 9px, 0.72px at 12px, 0.96px at 16px (a constant +0.06em)
- **Role:** This is the metadata layer of a film slate: eyebrows, counters, filter chips and the search field, always uppercase and set solid at 1.0 line height. Its 204 uses at 12px make it the second workhorse. The +0.06em tracking mirrors the grotesk's -0.02em in the opposite direction. The pairing creates a two-pole system where hierarchy comes from family and case, not from weight.

### Arial — the third-party consent layer, outside the brand system · `--font-arial`

- **Substitute:** Arimo at 400, Liberation Sans at 400
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 700
- **Sizes:** 14px, 16px, 18px
- **Line height:** 1.33 (18px), 1.71 (14px)
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at all sizes
- **Role:** Arial appears only inside the cookie opt-out dialog (10 uses) and as the inherited wrapper default on stat pills. It is an injected vendor component, not a brand decision. Reproduce it only when rebuilding the consent layer.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | PP Neue Montreal Mono | 400 | 9px | 1.0 | 0.54px | `--text-small` |
| caption | PP Neue Montreal Mono | 400 | 12px | 1.0 | 0.72px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Swizzy | 400 | 16px | 1.0 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Swizzy | 500 | 24px | 1.1 | -0.48px | `--text-body` |
| subheading | Swizzy | 500 | 32px | 1.0 | -0.64px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Swizzy | 700 | 38px | 1.16 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Swizzy | 500 | 58px | 1.1 | -1.16px | `--text-heading` |
| display | Swizzy | 500 | 160px | 0.86 | -3.2px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every Swizzy size from 24px up at weight 500 with -0.02em tracking — hierarchy comes from size alone, which is the signature.
- Pair each Swizzy headline with a 12px PP Neue Montreal Mono eyebrow at +0.06em, uppercase — the two-pole contrast is the whole typographic system.
- Use #141414 as the only filled action color, on both the 8px hero CTA and the 4px nav chip — the chromatic budget for actions is non-negotiable at zero hues.
- Tile film stills edge to edge at 0px radius inside a 16px #f5f5f5 frame — the round corner belongs to the container, the frames stay square like a contact sheet.
- Separate sections with 100px of white #ffffff, stepping to 180px before a display headline — space is the divider, not rules.
- Put #fecc33, #21935b and #30a81d only inside Inline Glyph Tiles or cursor avatars — color behaves like a grease-pencil mark.
- Draw graph-paper grids with #e9e9e9 lines on #f5f5f5 — the line work is tonal and never exceeds a one-step contrast.

### Don't

- Don't add a brand-yellow #fecc33 button because it is the most visible hue — it turns a decorative mark into a competitor for the film stills.
- Don't bold headlines to weight 700 for emphasis at 58px or 160px — the thesis of size-only hierarchy collapses once weight starts carrying meaning.
- Don't fill the space between 58px and 160px with intermediate 80px or 96px headings — the 2.76× leap is the drama, and a smooth ladder flattens it.
- Don't round still tiles to 16px or add gutters of 8px between them — the grid stops reading as a contact sheet and becomes a card gallery.
- Don't set body copy at a conventional 16px — Flim's paragraph voice is 24px Swizzy at 1.1, and shrinking it loses the editorial register.
- Don't put drop shadows on cards or the mockup frame — the only shadows are a 10px upward sm and the 68px xl on floating overlays, and everything else relies on #f5f5f5 tonal lift.
- Don't use mono in lowercase or with negative tracking — PP Neue Montreal Mono is never anything but uppercase at +0.06em, or it reads as code rather than slate metadata.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- secondary surface: #f5f5f5 (Fog Surface)
- grid lines and chips: #e9e9e9 (Mist Rule)
- primary text: #141414 (Ink)
- decorative accent: #fecc33 (Sunbeam Dot)
- presence marker: #30a81d (Sprout Signal)
- primary action: #141414 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts and counters stay neutral, with #141414 bars or pills on #f5f5f5 and #e9e9e9 grid lines, and #fecc33 allowed only as a single highlighted data point at 100% fill. Any surrounding film imagery stays the most colorful element.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: background #141414, text #ffffff, no border, border-radius 8px, padding 6px 16px 6px 6px, total height 44px. At left, place a 32px square image on a #fecc33 background with 4px radius. Follow it with a 12px gap and the label "SIGN UP NOW" in PP Neue Montreal Mono (fallback Geist Mono) at 12px, weight 400, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.72px, line-height 1.0. No shadow. On hover, swap the thumbnail image only, and do not change the fill color.

2. Build a hero section on #ffffff with max-width 1920px and 16px side padding. In a two-column split, the left column holds the word "Flim" in Swizzy (fallback Inter Display at 600) at 160px, weight 500, line-height 0.86, letter-spacing -3.2px, color #141414. The right column starts at the cap line and holds three lines of Swizzy at 24px, weight 500, line-height 1.1, letter-spacing -0.48px, followed after 32px by the Primary Action Button. Below, add a full-width #f5f5f5 band 464px tall with a 20px graph-paper grid of 1px #e9e9e9 lines, and the Search Well centered 52px from its bottom edge.

3. Build a Search Well: a container with background #e9e9e9, border-radius 32px, padding 6px, width 288px. Inside, add a transparent input 56px tall with no border, text #141414 in PP Neue Montreal Mono at 16px, weight 400, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.96px, and placeholder "SEARCH ANYTHING". Dock a button on the right with background #ffffff, text #141414, border-radius 64px, padding 12px 16px, same mono font at 16px, labelled "SEARCH ⌘/". No shadows anywhere.

4. Build a product mockup card: an outer frame with background #f5f5f5, border-radius 16px, overflow hidden, and a toolbar padded 24px. The toolbar holds the wordmark, a search field, and filter chips (background #e9e9e9, border-radius 160px, padding 4px 12px, PP Neue Montreal Mono 9px weight 400 uppercase, letter-spacing 0.54px, color #141414). Beneath it, a 12px mono counter reads "SHOWING 20 OF 11,286". Then place a 4-column grid of film stills with 0px gap and 0px radius, some tiles spanning 2×2. No shadow.

5. Build a section statement: a centered eyebrow "WHAT IS FLIM" in PP Neue Montreal Mono 12px weight 400 uppercase, letter-spacing 0.72px, #141414. After 52px, add two centered lines of Swizzy at 58px, weight 500, line-height 1.1, letter-spacing -1.16px, #141414. Inline within the text, place 58px square tiles with background #f5f5f5 and 0px radius showing a #fecc33 circle and #21935b double play arrows. Give the section 100px of space above and below.

### Ink Thumbnail Button — Primary

**Role:** Hero sign-up call to action

### Pill Search Button — White (Secondary)

**Role:** Submit inside the search well

A white capsule in a gray groove. Background #ffffff, text #141414, no border, border-radius 64px, padding 12px 16px, set in PP Neue Montreal Mono at 16px, weight 400, uppercase, 0.96px tracking, showing the label plus a ⌘/ shortcut, no shadow. **Role:** Compact account entry in header

**Role:** Top index of sections

The Flim wordmark sits at left, uppercase links spread across the width in Swizzy at 16px weight 400 #141414, and LOG-IN plus the Sign-Up Chip sit at right. The drawer variant sets the same links in #ffffff on #141414 with padding 6px 0 6px 14px. No shadow and no border are used. Navigation behaves like a table of contents rather than a toolbar.

### Product Mockup Frame

**Role:** Main content card, app preview

A contact sheet in a tray. Background #f5f5f5, no border, border-radius 16px on the outer frame (bottom corners on the image block), padding 24px around the toolbar, and no shadow. Inside, film stills tile edge to edge at 0px radius with zero gutter, under a 12px mono counter ("SHOWING 20 OF 11,286") and 9px mono filter chips. This is the system's main card, and the radius belongs to the frame, never the frames.

### Search Well

**Role:** Primary query input on hero

A recessed capsule. Container background #e9e9e9 (estimated), border-radius 32px, padding 6px, input height 56px, no border, placeholder and value in #141414 set in PP Neue Montreal Mono at 16px, weight 400, uppercase, 0.96px tracking, with the white Pill Search Button docked right, and no shadow. Centered low on the graph-paper hero, it frames search as the product's single verb.

### Stat Pill Badge

**Role:** Library size counters

Inked capsules for numbers. Background #141414, text #ffffff, border-radius 160px, padding 24px, height 74px, with labels such as 400K videos, 5.8K movies and 150K animations. The wrapper computes Arial at 16px weight 400 as an inherited default, so rebuild the label in Swizzy at 24px weight 500 with -0.48px tracking. The 160px radius is a deliberate pill outlier that marks these as data, not actions.

### Genre Filter Tab

**Role:** Mood and genre switcher

Bare typographic tabs. No background, text #141414, no border, border-radius 0px, padding 12px 0, width 168px, height 40px, set in Swizzy at 16px, weight 400, uppercase labels such as NOIR, GIALLO and SCI-FI, no shadow. Selection is carried by type and position rather than a filled chip. That restraint is anti-convention for filter UI and keeps the stills as the only loud element.

### Filter Chip — Mockup Toolbar

**Role:** Facet filters inside product

Small gray capsules. Background #e9e9e9, text #141414, no border, border-radius 160px, padding 4px 12px, set in PP Neue Montreal Mono at 9px, weight 400, uppercase, 0.54px tracking, no shadow, with labels such as Video, Motion, Genre and Frame Ratio. These are the only place the 9px step appears. They signal dense metadata at contact-sheet scale.

### Section Eyebrow

**Role:** Section index labels

A slate marking. No background, text #141414, set in PP Neue Montreal Mono at 12px, weight 400, uppercase, 0.72px tracking, line height 1.0, placed 52px above a Swizzy headline, with examples such as WHAT IS FLIM, DATABASE and TRUSTED BY THE BRANDS SHAPING CULTURE. The eyebrow is the system's chapter number, and it is always mono so the grotesk below can stay pure.

### Inline Glyph Tile

**Role:** Pictograms set inside headlines

Punctuation rather than decoration. A #f5f5f5 square with #e9e9e9 graph-paper lines and border-radius 0px sits inline at headline cap height inside 58px Swizzy text. It holds a #fecc33 disc, a #21935b double play arrow, or a wider word highlight. These tiles are the only sanctioned home for saturated color in the editorial layer, so the accent arrives as a glyph, not a fill.

### Logo Marquee Row

**Role:** Client trust strip

A monochrome credits roll. Logos for clients such as Logitech, Hermès, Apple, Chanel and Partizan render as 34px-tall images in #141414 on #ffffff, scrolling horizontally with 64px gaps under a 12px mono eyebrow, at 0px radius with no containers or shadow. Stripping brand colors from the logos keeps the chromatic budget intact.

### Opt-Out Consent Dialog — System Outlier

**Role:** Third-party privacy preferences

An imported vendor panel. Background #ffffff, body text #212121 (not a system token), border-radius 2px on buttons and checkbox, button height 42px with padding 8px, and a Cancel button with a 1px #000000 border (not a system token). The save button is filled #fe3600 (third-party, not a system token), type is Arial at 14px weights 400 and 500, and the panel carries shadow xl. It breaks the shape, color and font rules and is allowed only because it is injected by the consent vendor.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every Swizzy size from 24px up at weight 500 with -0.02em tracking — hierarchy comes from size alone, which is the signature.
- Pair each Swizzy headline with a 12px PP Neue Montreal Mono eyebrow at +0.06em, uppercase — the two-pole contrast is the whole typographic system.
- Use #141414 as the only filled action color, on both the 8px hero CTA and the 4px nav chip — the chromatic budget for actions is non-negotiable at zero hues.
- Tile film stills edge to edge at 0px radius inside a 16px #f5f5f5 frame — the round corner belongs to the container, the frames stay square like a contact sheet.
- Separate sections with 100px of white #ffffff, stepping to 180px before a display headline — space is the divider, not rules.
- Put #fecc33, #21935b and #30a81d only inside Inline Glyph Tiles or cursor avatars — color behaves like a grease-pencil mark.
- Draw graph-paper grids with #e9e9e9 lines on #f5f5f5 — the line work is tonal and never exceeds a one-step contrast.

### Don't

- Don't add a brand-yellow #fecc33 button because it is the most visible hue — it turns a decorative mark into a competitor for the film stills.
- Don't bold headlines to weight 700 for emphasis at 58px or 160px — the thesis of size-only hierarchy collapses once weight starts carrying meaning.
- Don't fill the space between 58px and 160px with intermediate 80px or 96px headings — the 2.76× leap is the drama, and a smooth ladder flattens it.
- Don't round still tiles to 16px or add gutters of 8px between them — the grid stops reading as a contact sheet and becomes a card gallery.
- Don't set body copy at a conventional 16px — Flim's paragraph voice is 24px Swizzy at 1.1, and shrinking it loses the editorial register.
- Don't put drop shadows on cards or the mockup frame — the only shadows are a 10px upward sm and the 68px xl on floating overlays, and everything else relies on #f5f5f5 tonal lift.
- Don't use mono in lowercase or with negative tracking — PP Neue Montreal Mono is never anything but uppercase at +0.06em, or it reads as code rather than slate metadata.

## Surfaces

| Level | Name | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | Page ground, marquee band, editorial sections |
| 1 | Fog Surface | `#f5f5f5` | Hero grid field, product mockup frame, glyph tiles |
| 2 | Mist Rule | `#e9e9e9` | Search well, filter chips, grid lines |
| 3 | Frosted Glass | `#ffffff1a` | Translucent chips layered on dark panels |
| 4 | Ink | `#141414` | Inverted CTA, stat pills, nav drawer, dark feature section |

## Elevation

- **Floating overlays and dialogs:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3) 0px 32px 68px 0px`
- **Bottom-docked bars casting upward:** `rgba(172, 171, 171, 0.3) 0px -1px 10px 0px`

Everything else is flat. Cards, buttons, pills and the mockup frame carry no shadow and rise only by tonal steps from #ffffff to #f5f5f5 to #e9e9e9. That is the opposite of the conventional card-shadow SaaS stack.

## Imagery

Imagery is real cinema: film stills from titles across genres, shown as a dense mosaic of square-cut frames with zero gutter inside a 16px-radius #f5f5f5 product frame. There is no border and no shadow, and footage carries every saturated color on the page. There is no stock photography and no 3D illustration. Icons are minimal: bold black ✖ marks scattered as editorial annotations, a ⌘/ shortcut glyph, and flat geometric pictograms (a #fecc33 disc, #21935b double play arrows) set in graph-paper tiles. The hero background is a #e9e9e9 graph-paper grid on #f5f5f5 rather than a gradient. No glows, orbs or gradients exist as system tokens. The narrative is an archivist's light table where the films do the talking.

## Layout

Content spans up to 1920px with 16px outer gutters (estimated from the left-aligned wordmark), so the 160px display runs nearly edge to edge. Sections are separated by 100px, stretching to 180px before display headlines, and the footer opens with 128px top padding. The hero splits asymmetrically: a giant Flim wordmark at left, and a 24px three-line pitch plus the Ink Thumbnail Button at right. Below it, a full-width graph-paper field holds the centered Search Well. Sections alternate white editorial blocks, a centered single-column 58px statement, a 4-column stills mosaic in the product frame, left-aligned 160px headings, and an Ink-filled feature section with white 160px type. The logo row is a single horizontal marquee. The nav is non-sticky and filled, about 38px tall (estimated), with the wordmark left and LOG-IN plus SIGN-UP right. The footer is a tall 1294px block led by a large tagline. At 375px, use the 58px heading step as display and 64px section gaps. Density: spacious.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- secondary surface: #f5f5f5 (Fog Surface)
- grid lines and chips: #e9e9e9 (Mist Rule)
- primary text: #141414 (Ink)
- decorative accent: #fecc33 (Sunbeam Dot)
- presence marker: #30a81d (Sprout Signal)
- primary action: #141414 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts and counters stay neutral, with #141414 bars or pills on #f5f5f5 and #e9e9e9 grid lines, and #fecc33 allowed only as a single highlighted data point at 100% fill. Any surrounding film imagery stays the most colorful element.

**Example Component Prompts**

On hover, swap the thumbnail image only, and do not change the fill color.

2. Build a hero section on #ffffff with max-width 1920px and 16px side padding. In a two-column split, the left column holds the word "Flim" in Swizzy (fallback Inter Display at 600) at 160px, weight 500, line-height 0.86, letter-spacing -3.2px, color #141414. The right column starts at the cap line and holds three lines of Swizzy at 24px, weight 500, line-height 1.1, letter-spacing -0.48px, followed after 32px by the Primary Action Button. Below, add a full-width #f5f5f5 band 464px tall with a 20px graph-paper grid of 1px #e9e9e9 lines, and the Search Well centered 52px from its bottom edge.

Inside, add a transparent input 56px tall with no border, text #141414 in PP Neue Montreal Mono at 16px, weight 400, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.96px, and placeholder "SEARCH ANYTHING". Dock a button on the right with background #ffffff, text #141414, border-radius 64px, padding 12px 16px, same mono font at 16px, labelled "SEARCH ⌘/". No shadows anywhere.

4. Build a product mockup card: an outer frame with background #f5f5f5, border-radius 16px, overflow hidden, and a toolbar padded 24px. The toolbar holds the wordmark, a search field, and filter chips (background #e9e9e9, border-radius 160px, padding 4px 12px, PP Neue Montreal Mono 9px weight 400 uppercase, letter-spacing 0.54px, color #141414). ## Polar Type Discipline

Flim's typography has two poles and no middle: Swizzy 500 at -0.02em for everything that speaks, and PP Neue Montreal Mono 400 uppercase at +0.06em for everything that labels. Size is the only hierarchy lever, from 24px body to the 160px display, with a deliberate 2.76× jump at the top. The discipline breaks the moment someone adds a third family for UI, sets body in 16px mono, or bolds a 58px line to separate it from its neighbor. To extend it, pick a size from the existing scale and keep the tracking rule. New metadata goes into mono at 12px or 9px, and new statements go into Swizzy at 24px, 32px, 58px or 160px, nothing in between.

## Footage Carries Color

The interface is effectively achromatic: #141414 on #ffffff with #f5f5f5 and #e9e9e9 as the only intermediate tones. The film stills therefore become the palette, and a Kurosawa red or a Villeneuve ochre lands with full force. The four decorative hues exist only as tiny glyphs, and the one bright button on the page (#fe3600) belongs to a third-party dialog. This breaks if a brand hue reaches a CTA, a section background, a hover state or a chart fill. To extend the system, add new UI in Ink and Fog, express emphasis through scale or inversion to #141414, and if a new accent is unavoidable, confine it to a 58px Inline Glyph Tile.

## Graph Paper Ground

Instead of gradients or shadows, Flim grounds its hero and glyph tiles on a drafting grid: 1px #e9e9e9 lines over #f5f5f5, square-cut, with no blur. It reads as a storyboard sheet, a production artifact rather than a marketing backdrop. The grid breaks if lines darken past #e9e9e9, if cells are rounded, or if it sits behind body copy and competes with 24px text. To extend it, use the grid only behind interactive focal points (search, glyphs, word highlights). Keep its cells on multiples of the 4px base, and let it end at hard section edges instead of fading out.

## Similar Brands

- **ShotDeck** — The same category of searchable film-still libraries for directors and agencies. ShotDeck leans on dark, dense UI, while Flim runs a white editorial canvas.
- **Cosmos** — Shares the monochrome interface that defers to user imagery and an uppercase-label metadata layer. Cosmos uses softer rounded cards where Flim keeps stills square.
- **Are.na** — Shares a near-black-on-white palette, mono uppercase labels and a refusal to add a brand color to actions.
- **Savee** — The same visual-reference search audience and edge-to-edge image mosaic. Flim adds 160px display typography that Savee does not use.
- **Teenage Engineering** — Shares the engineering-slate pairing of grotesk plus mono with color rationed to small geometric glyphs and dots.
